'''''Zephyranthes robusta''''',  commonly known as the '''Brazilian copperlily''', '''pink fairy lily''' or the '''pink rain lily''', is a species of herbaceous flowering bulb in the family ''[[Amaryllidaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:270986-2 |title= Zephyranthes robusta (Herb.) Baker |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=November 30, 2024}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/7YFJX |title= Zephyranthes robusta (Herb.) Baker |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=November 30, 2024}}</ref> It is native to [[Brazil]], [[Argentina]] and [[Uruguay]],<ref name=Mathew1987>{{Citation |last=Mathew |first=Brian |year=1987 |title=The Smaller Bulbs |location=London |publisher=B.T. Batsford |isbn=978-0-7134-4922-8 }}, p. 101</ref> but is now naturalized in Florida, Colombia, South Africa, and Mauritius.<ref>[https://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=276741 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[https://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Habranthus%20robustus.png Biota of North America Program]</ref>

==Description==
''Zephyranthes robusta'' is a relatively large species of rain lily. It grows from [[wikt:ovate|ovate]] to [[wikt:obovate|obovate]] [[bulb]]s around {{convert|3.5|to|5|cm|abbr=on}} in diameter.<ref name="araujo">{{cite journal|author1=Anderson Alves-Araújo|author2=Julie Henriette Antoinette Dutilh|author3=Marccus Alves|year=2009|title=Amaryllidaceae s.s. e Alliaceae s.s. no Nordeste Brasileiro|journal=Rodriguésia|volume=60|issue=2|pages=311–331|language=Portuguese|publisher=Instituto de Pesquisas Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro|doi=10.1590/2175-7860200960206|issn=0370-6583|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Plants bear solitary lavender to pale pink, funnel-shaped flowers, {{convert|5|–|6|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, held at a slight angle on {{convert|15|–|30|cm|in|abbr=on}} [[Scape (botany)|scape]]s,<ref name=Mathew1987/> with a leaf-like [[bract]] {{convert|1.8|–|4|cm|in|abbr=on}} long at the base. Flowers typically appear after rain from late summer to early fall and are followed by large deep green leaves, measuring {{convert|5|to|10|mm|in|abbr=on}} wide and {{convert|30|to|40|cm|abbr=on}} long.<ref name="colombia"/>

==Taxonomy and nomenclature==
[[File:Habranthus robustus (2).jpg|thumb|left|150px|''H. robustus'' from [[Florida]].]]
[[File:Habranthus robustus (3).jpg|thumb|''H. robustus'' have declineate slightly asymmetrical flowers.]]
''Zephyranthes robusta'' belongs to the genus ''[[Zephyranthes]]'' (rain lilies)  of the [[tribe (biology)|tribe]] [[Hippeastreae]],<ref name=GarcMeerArroOliv19>{{Cite journal |last1=García |first1=Nicolás |last2=Meerow |first2=Alan W. |last3=Arroyo‐Leuenberger |first3=Silvia |last4=Oliveira |first4=Renata S. |last5=Dutilh |first5=Julie H. |last6=Soltis |first6=Pamela S. |last7=Judd |first7=Walter S. |date=2019 |title=Generic classification of Amaryllidaceae tribe Hippeastreae |journal=Taxon |volume=68 |issue=3 |pages=481–498 |doi=10.1002/tax.12062 |s2cid=202854432 |name-list-style=amp }}</ref> within the [[subfamily]] [[Amaryllidoideae]] of the amaryllis family ([[Amaryllidaceae]]). In older classifications, it was sometimes included within the lily family ([[Liliaceae]]).<ref name="GRIN"/> Once treated as ''Habranthus robustus'', it is now re-included in ''Zephyranthes''.<ref name=POWO/><ref name=GarcMeerArroOliv19/>

It is commonly known as the 'pink fairy lily', 'pink rain lily', 'pink zephyr lily', 'pink magic lily', 'pink fawn lily', and 'Colombian mini-amaryllis'. It is known as ''cebollita'' in [[Spanish language|Spanish]].

Due to having the same common names, it is also frequently confused with other 'pink rain lilies' - namely ''[[Zephyranthes rosea]]'' and ''[[Zephyranthes carinata]]'' (also sold under the name ''Zephyranthes grandiflora''). The three species are often mislabeled, but ''Z. robusta'' is easily recognizable from the other two by its larger, more strongly bent (and often asymmetrical), paler pink flowers.<ref name="yuccado">{{cite web|url=http://www.yuccado.com/article_rain_lilies/|title=Rain Lily Log - June|publisher=YuccaDo Nursery Inc.|access-date=August 7, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110902044243/http://www.yuccado.com/article_rain_lilies|archive-date=September 2, 2011}}</ref> ''Z. robusta'' also has leaves covered with a fine grayish waxy coating (glaucous) in contrast to the leaves of ''Z. carinata''.<ref name="colombia"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Zephyranthes robusta'' is believed to have originated from [[Rio Grande do Sul]] of [[Brazil]]. It is [[native species|native]] to [[Brazil]], [[Argentina]], and [[Uruguay]], and is widely [[naturalized species|naturalized]] elsewhere.<ref name="colombia">{{cite journal|author1=José Luis Fernández-Alonso|author2=Jeroen P. Groenendijk|year=2004|title=A New Species of ''Zephyranthes'' Herb. S. L. (Amaryllidaceae, Hippeastreae), with Notes on the Genus in Colombia|journal=Rev. Acad. Colomb. Cienc.|volume=28|issue=107|pages=177–186|issn=0370-3908|url=http://www.accefyn.org.co/revista/Vol_28/107/177-186.pdf|accessdate=August 7, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111001060544/http://www.accefyn.org.co/revista/Vol_28/107/177-186.pdf|archive-date=October 1, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Cultivation and uses==
''Zephyranthes robusta'' is widely grown as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental]]. It is one of the most prolific of the summer flowering rain lilies. They are propagated by dividing the [[bulb]]s (including offsets) and from seed. They are not as tolerant of colder temperatures as other rain lilies.<ref name="knox">{{cite journal|author=Gary W. Knox|year=2005|title=Rainlily, ''Zephyranthes'' and ''Habranthus'' spp.: Low Maintenance Flowering Bulbs for Florida Gardens|journal=Enh1151|publisher=Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences Extension, University of Florida|url=http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/pdffiles/EP/EP41200.pdf|accessdate=August 7, 2011|archive-date=September 26, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926111604/http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/pdffiles/EP/EP41200.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Chemical composition==
<!-- including all components make it large, only try to include alkaloids and remove others if found except for other compounds that have significant health effects -->
The plant contains some toxic compounds like [[lycorine]]. Other compound include [[galanthamine]], [[3-epimacronine]], [[hippeastidine]], [[lycoramine]], [[galanthine]], [[haemanthamine]], [[haemanthidine]], [[hamayne]], [[tazettine]], [[vittatine]], [[11-hydroxy vittatine]], [[8-O-demethylmaritidine]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.longdom.org/open-access/phytochemistry-and-pharmacology-of-genus-zephyranthes-2167-0412-1000212.pdf|title=Katoch D and Singh B, Med Aromat Plants}}</ref>

==Toxicity==
Similar to the closely related species of ''[[Zephyranthes]]'', ''Z. robusta'' contains toxic [[alkaloid]]s. Mainly [[galantamine]]-type alkaloids which can be lethal for humans.<ref name="bjp">{{cite journal|author1=Lucie Cahlíková|author2=Irena Valterová|author3=Kateřina Macáková|author4=Lubomír Opletal|year=2010|title=Analysis of Amaryllidaceae alkaloids from ''Zephyranthes grandiflora'' by GC/MS and their cholinesterase activity|journal=Brazilian Journal of Pharmacognosy (Revista Brasileira de Farmacognosia)|volume=5|issue=8|pages=1201–1204|publisher=Sociedade Brasileira de Farmacognosia|issn=0102-695X|url=http://www.scielo.br/pdf/rbfar/2011nahead/aop8711.pdf|accessdate=August 7, 2011|archive-date=October 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121013071020/http://www.scielo.br/pdf/rbfar/2011nahead/aop8711.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
